clusters.root_cause: Both tests install a BEFORE INSERT trigger on `circus.circus_run_projection` that `RAISE EXCEPTION 'test projection failure'`. The PostgresException bubbles up out of the trigger and the IngestionTransaction rolls back, satisfying the atomicity invariant (the journal row is gone and the projection is gone). The `IngestEventService` then maps the unhandled PostgresException to `PersistenceFailure UnexpectedDatabaseFailure` only when the exception flows through the typed classification; under the trigger path the typed mapper does not recognise P0001 and the test's `match ... | PersistenceFailure _` arm is not taken, the test then `failwithf`s with the projected state. The trigger is the deliberate cause; the gap is that `UnexpectedDatabaseFailure` is reported as a typed result by the first test (which passes) but the second test (typed AppendFailed rollback) sees a raw PostgresException because the typed `PersistenceFailure` constructor is not produced on this path. Both tests are therefore correctly observing an untyped P0001 escape where the contract expected a typed result.
clusters.evidence_basis: raw-test-output.txt lines 166-182, 285-301; ConcurrencyTests.fs:220-260; AppendFailedRollbackTests.fs:183-216; src/Circus.Persistence.Postgres/IngestionTransaction.fs (typed classification of NpgsqlException)

clusters.minimal_reproduction_observed: Pending isolated run; failure observed in raw-test-output.txt lines 302-329
clusters.root_cause: tests/Circus.Persistence.Postgres.Tests/SemanticReplayTests.fs:79-85 ingests a compact request then a `reorderedTopRequest`. The reordered form (Support.fs:163-189) swaps the `id` and `source` keys in the JSON, producing a different raw_body (the bytes themselves are reordered) and therefore a different SHA-256 digest. The production idempotent-replay path matches on (source, event_id, raw_body_sha256) and treats a digest mismatch as EventIdentityConflict, not as a replay. The test expects the production code to consider only the canonical event identity (source, event_id) and to be a replay for any same-identity follow-up regardless of body bytes. The test's three sibling tests (whitespace, nested-data, nested-checks) all use the same logical identity and identical body (modulo whitespace/key reorder that does not change byte length/digest), and they pass; only the top-level-keys reorder changes the byte-level digest, so the test author likely intended the production code to ignore the byte-level reorder. The current contract is: idempotent replay only when raw_body_sha256 matches.
